title: 5–6 september
author: samayra
text:
this is not january 19, and not 2024. it is not a diary entry that i thought i would write here. except my wishes never come true, similar to the typo i made here. is it called that even when the person is writing this manually? i don’t think that’s a word. my writing is becoming more inspired by, or inclined towards, technical words. for a person who thought she could keep her thoughts and her work in different spectrums, witnessing those colours merge is giving me no joy, though. as if finally, all my theories, philosophies, and aspirations are waking up, calling me out to wake up — or just to stop daydreaming. this is not the only side of my life where i have confronted myself with being wrong. there is no surprise when these things turn out to be what they actually are. how many times would a girl wish upon a breaking, falling star? you are hopeless, free-falling under a planet you know nothing about. realizing this doesn’t make me stop wishing again, though. but this time, i wish to aspire a little less. as if it might come true. i am finally sick. sick as i always was. no one wants to talk about their weakness, but i am not talking, am i? i am writing it here. nobody will read this again. i don’t think i will. this diary is old, and even though the metal binding makes it look regal, it is difficult to write here. i was always sick. the last time was today in the morning, when i got a fever. feverish enough to feel the shivers run through my body. my face planted on the pillow, which i hated the day i came here. closed my ears, which were feeling heavy despite removing my earrings a few weeks earlier. hollow. empty. hearing the white noise of the fan cutting the air into slices and shapes. i am listening to a youtube playlist of an hour-long timeline to avoid ads. the channel has a few hundred subscribers, with some thousand views here and there. i always wondered who these people were. how they thought of opening a channel just like that. recently, i watched *sterling point*, where, after a one-night stand, she says she might be “going on a spree or a crisis, doing things she never thought she could,” stating that someone should stop her when she opens a youtube channel. i gave a hollow laugh, advising my thoughts to approve of her. to realize that some things are cool only to some people. days here are not linear. i remember eating bread two days ago and calling it a thursday. i open a book i finished a few days ago, realizing it’s already over. she is already in the hospital, delivering her daughter, who is just 7 lbs. i thought about writing about the book i read — writing as in publishing it online — but my lack of proof, of feeling like an imposter claiming to be a writer or a “blogger,” has limited me to an already-lacking undercurrent in the river where i swam occasionally, seldomly making myself new again. there is no definite timeline. i don’t see the way i will ever be back there. even writing here, i am already analyzing, convincing myself that if i see something good, something that matches my statue of marble on the internet, made of just 22 rules, maybe then i will feel that it would be something. my mother said that when i was sick, when i was earliest, i was born sick. kept under the blue light, which i no longer recall, kept there for a week with kids like me. born too early here. unhappy and sick. it is the fifth of september, 2026, when i am writing this. my fever is down now, just a few degrees below what it was, but normal. my mother is not here to count 60. my father is not here, clicking his fingers on the car key. i see the timestamp in numbers cross 61 seconds on the screen, closing my eyes and seeing 99 on the digital screen. i think i can write more, but i don’t want to. just like i know i can make this life worthwhile, but don’t have any desire to. there is everything i could do in this world. the world is of endless possibilities. someone is out there solving data-storing methods in bacterial DNA, someone is in her bed, listening to Gracie Abrams with the shared album of her roommate, learning ADME processes because her playlists are too depressing. my fever is almost gone, cough is still here, knocking my head against a wall isn’t working anymore, sneezing is, well, the meds work. that’s all i could say. the results came, my immune system, which was a great topic of discussion from yesterday, was not good. i already knew this, but seeing it again wasn’t a good sight, seeing it way under the normal range, highlighted in bold on my screen. hospitals are weird, seeing parents drag their crying toddlers with bags and sippers, witnessing older parents being dragged around by their offspring in wheelchairs, waiting for elevators, recognizing every stop where my hands or clothes touched. sitting on my chair, tired from the ride, cleaning my desk and chair with wet wipes. in the first blog, i said i would continue this till i turn a year older. i didn’t give much context to the blog thing and why i am writing it. i am turning a year older this coming week, which is just a few days away. i remember when i was 14, i scheduled an email to myself for when i would be 43. i don’t know why that age. i thought at that time, maybe this will be the age when i would do everything and would obviously forget what a 14-year-old me ever was, including her whimsical dreams and rock-band obsessions. somewhere, along the way of writing this, i remember asking my mother about her teenage years. she remembers, i guess, in bits, and maybe that’s why i chose this. i don’t remember her. nor do i want to open the email in my drafts to uncover the suspense. so, why am i writing this? just a way i would remember. remember writing that i forget, that even i forget. there is somewhere else, a place i can visit to just remember.

title: Am i still in august?
author: samayra
text:
22/08/2026

This is not the day I write in this document. I had the writing in my journal. After arranging my shelf for the fifth time since the day I came here, I found this page, again tucked in the corner. But this time, I didn’t remember how I put it there.

Maybe I have more memories to hold onto now, or just less time to give meaning to things that I always thought I wanted.

> All said and done, I want my childhood back, the innocence of having something experienced for the first time, but I never wanted it to return; it was the past, and I am not her anymore. I hate expectations, hate ideals, and hate promises that are never fulfilled.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/1024/0*X0qfjSjKpDWU1gvS.jpeg)

coco commented : i can feel and smell this image good job

26/08/2026

When I started writing this document today, the text started in the colour white, hidden inside the colour of the background page itself. I deleted what I wrote earlier, just the usual lie I tell in all my truths: that I write less these days.

These days here are like songs in my liked playlist on Spotify. No arrangement, no theme, like the sorted one I had in the past. I feel every day like a new tune from my favourite artist, praying that it will be good, better than the last, and better than the last day.

I talk to my parents with my headphones on, I talk to my hostel warden with my earbuds on, nodding along to the rules I know nothing about, and my room has a speaker or a soundbox thing that plays different tunes like “calm,” “ocean,” “forest,” and wait, let me get it — there is “rain,” “relax,” and “white noise” too.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/735/0*RAvY-J2phVGU318V.jpeg)

skrunkly commented : I like the title, I feel like it describes how to feel all over the place, and the clothing tossed all over the floor kind of matches that feeling

I like the forest track in the morning. Haven’t tried the ocean and white noise yet. This one is new in that sense.

I remember how, some time ago, I wasn’t able to sleep properly; the birds in the dusk were the only reason I was able to sleep for a few hours till the morning came and made my dreams unreal.

Last month, on this day, I was with my parents. Yesterday, I talked for around 2 hours before dinner, and after that, since the mess would close soon, we talked for an hour more.

I am talking more, more in the sense that I never talked much in the first place. The song is still playing now; the voice is familiar in a sense.

I have started singing again.

title: i will write this again.
author: samayra
text:
![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/736/0*2GUvySk_XjW6B_wb.jpeg)

Время идёт, а я всё живу с одним чувством, которое испытал много лет назад

I have been playing a game recently to distract myself from the impending doom coming like a crisis in my life. I am recalling my past memories, asking my mom questions about whether the timeline fits or not. I am trying to recall my earliest memory.

The game is simple: you pick a memory while playing a heavy sentimental song, you close your eyes, it should be dark, or just cover them with your sweatshirt lying around. Take deep breaths, open a linked song is what I recommend, to avoid ads in between. Remember anything from yesterday, like the coffee cup you left on the table, or when your pen fell down, and you bent to pick it up… just things you think you remember doing every day. But in this memory, you remember yourself more clearly, remembering the exact clothes you wore, the way your hair was pinned at the back, the shirt riding up or coming loose. I swear it will be like watching a movie.

Then continue with any of your school days. Maybe it will be the last day you watched yourself. For me, it was the last day in school. I went to my class, the lights were off, except for the afternoon sun lying leisurely beyond the hills, awaiting for me to open the door, grab my bag, and take out my notes for the school-end speech. The corridor was so quiet, the classroom was filled with memories and breaths so heavy, and I felt helpless, helpless in a way that I ran, ran back to the amphitheatre where the ending ceremony was going on, sitting in my seat, watching teachers talk about things, things that are no longer in my memory, neither the words I spoke nor what was said to me.

My mother said I was never good with endings. She recalled whenever we left Nani Ma’s house during holidays, how I used to cry the most, returning back, making myself sleep the whole journey back. To hold the truth between us, I remember nothing from this. I never remembered myself not liking endings.

For the next step, you need someone, a memory of someone, a face you have already forgotten, the name now just a few letters, remembering only whether they were in your class or not, during exams taking your guess on the roll number before the name itself.

I remember the first day in my new school. The air was filled with July rain, heavy clouds resting above the green grass, someone pronouncing my name wrong before they ever learnt it. A few years later, telling me I was selfish. A year after that, never speaking to me again.

I applaud myself for forgetting it. I hate myself for remembering only the parts where there was hate and never love.

I have lived my life in blue doors. Now the one I have is beige. No character, no association, a uniform unlike my dramatic self that needs something to be a metaphor for her, explain her emotions, be a medium to channelise her thoughts, in a way, a person has to remove the sheer curtains, knowing that it’s morning, but just to check whether the sun, where it always is, is there or not.

The things I did to distract myself surely worked. I haven’t written in… it’s long enough for me to scroll past all the notes I posted on Substack, the feature to which I called names, and liked people who talked badly about it. I even posted a trademark note about how good this feature is. It was satire. I believed only my few true readers must have picked it up, if not, people I am mean, but not that much. Admitting this doesn’t make me cool, or selfish. Maybe it does, in a way that I care not much about anymore.

Good news is, I’m in college, and the bad news is washing clothes is hard, more hard than cutting fruits by yourself. I have been using claw clips, a hair accessory I thought only belonged to mothers. (I am wrong here; it’s just that, in a household of three women, my mother always used claw clips. The rubber bands were just for us, and despite having an elder sister, she never used one, or did, just that I haven’t seen it.)

I took three books with me. One is this physics one, the other is *The Alchemist* (just because it has a pen-down note from my father), and the first *Harry Potter* book I ever read. It is brown, torn down. I travelled with it in my backpack instead of the carry-on; it would have fitted perfectly in it. I purchased some more books here, normal ones. I like my room, the food is passable, blinkit is just ten minutes here, and the vending machine is actively playing tricks with my money-managing cells, to make myself broke one day.

The first day I arrived in Delhi was just a day after I turned sixteen. I had a rover with me, which was already sent away for exhibition. I had a blue suitcase, a small old backpack, where the cake I cut in the train rested in the transparent plastic box. I didn’t eat the cake afterwards. I didn’t win anything there, even. The day I returned back from Delhi, I gave my Class 10 pre-board Maths paper in the afternoon, in which I scored 96.

It is not that I never thought I would never be back here; my relatives live here. It is just that when I arrived here again, I didn’t know how to book a cab here. We could have a peepal tree or an ATM in Ajmeri Gate.

The next time I came here, though, it was a simple cab ride from the airport, nothing dramatic.

While recalling this, I remember whatever has transpired these whole two weeks, and I feel this memory is enough as it is, without adding a layer to it about me writing this. This is special; it would hold more meaning if I said these things to someone.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/736/0*X2dhGqtP5s33oM5e.jpeg)

*I don’t know who I am without them.*

*Them. A man in his early fifties, married for thirty years to a woman now in her mid-forties. They have two daughters, the elder one twenty-two. They have no idea who I am becoming. And perhaps that’s why I don’t know who I am without them. It is one in the morning, and they have just left. I know how long it will take for them to reach the hotel, I know the cab they are in now, I know the intersection they have already passed by now, I close my eyes and I know that if I call them now, just now instead of writing this, they will turn back.*

a draft of drafts, i am sorry that it has no structure.

title: 8:01 PM POETRY
author: samayra
text:
JULY 2026

I have lived behind blue doors.  
 Blue skies folded over blush concrete.  
 Tomorrow will be the day  
 I will no longer be anywhere.

Old playlists will remain unplayed.  
 I am new, I will tell my old self.  
 A new song, an unreleased album, will await.  
 I will hold myself close. I am still here.

I will cry and shout. I will sing the tune again,  
 telling myself I am not the only one.

I will call, save the numbers of strangers.  
 I will remember, reminding myself:  
 one tear, one day, just enough.

I will reach out to say something,  
 meaning everything,  
 meaning nothing.

I know you are on the other end,  
 the end back home, back to you.

title: Am i still in july?
author: samayra
text:
**24/07/2026**

It is July, and Jennie’s new song, A Little Less Than a Lover, is on loop in my ears. I have been procrastinating since last week, avoiding some important articles while cramming maths like a human I no longer recognise. As I write this, I realise that the last time I wrote in this document was in June, and now July is coming to an end. Before I was going to write this, I wondered why some months have 30 and 31 days, like why August has 31 but not September. It explained that the reason is an amalgam of superstitions of Romans and their imperial vanity. Julius Caesar (the month of July was named after him) gave July thirty-one days because it was named after him, and Augustus, the jealous fellow, wanted his month, August, to have thirty-one days too.

Writing is hard these days. Not as liberating as it once was. Life keeps interrupting the sentence. I have become way too curious about real life, and I have no exams for the time being, yet no words seem to come through.

So, my writing regimen has reduced to a bliss I fathomed in a fortnight, but this time, it was a month later. The world has a lot going on too; the world has finally become a participating factor in what I do, maybe in one way instead of the backdrop I barely glance at, continuing my act. Perhaps I am allowing myself to feel things I once ignored.

I have been taking decisions; I am afraid of making decisions.

When my sister was here last month, I asked her how you can just do things. She looked at me funny, but I couldn’t explain more. I am afraid of making wrong decisions. I am afraid of finding truths that I no longer see, finding lies I will never uncover and learning more about myself in these situations where I end up hating myself instead of loving.

What if I am not normal? What if the shell I lived in until now was a better place? What should I not do? What do you think will happen to me? How do you just live? Is it scary? Is it normal to have so many questions? I think I am scared; I realise this again and again while writing this. Maybe she did it too, taking me in a hug.

I miss you.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/744/1*Yg6f5hrTy7lcG3DjSqKfyg.jpeg)

pin

**25/07/2026**

It is a Saturday, and after months I am waiting for a Sunday the way I used to. In the school where I spent most of my primary education, the classes were only held until midday. I only liked that day mainly because it was activity day and every period extended a little more than usual, longer and less tiring.

I always find myself in these situations where I want to continue just a little more; I don’t want it to end, but even if it were definite, just not now. Maybe the song I am listening to shouldn’t linger after playing but just play for a few seconds more. In these seconds maybe I will cherish it more and miss it somewhat less.

Later at school, I further transitioned, making Saturdays the same as another weekday. On those Saturdays, I missed myself, who was in third grade, finger painting on a white sheet with her classmates, then standing on the wooden table, pinning up the chart paper on the maroon velvet cushion board and, with paint still left on her hands, chasing her friends in blue hallways and white stairs, feeling sick because of the smell of vinegar and baking soda on school exhibition projects.

I know when I changed; I think that it was my misery. These memories never arrive in waves; the waves in the years until now I learned or conditioned myself to surf.

I still remember the sea, how I slipped my unlucky foot, just twelve, opening my eyes finally, seeing nothing and everything with my eyes burning, licking my lips, tasting salt, and how I was lifted above by my armpits, told it was time to go back and that I could come back tomorrow. I haven’t been to the sea since that day.

My tomorrow never came.

title: I am another being.
author: samayra
text:
I am another being. I am no longer what I used to be. I am no one and everyone. I am just another human being.

For reasons that are unknown to you and known only to me, I have arrived at a place in my life where I am no one. I am not the girl I used to be, nor will I be the woman I once imagined. When I write this, I realise how many circles I have just looped in my head to avoid telling you the truth. And in these moments I realise that some parts of my past are still with me. The parts where I wrote to tell everyone how I have become a liar and how I don’t want to write all my truths anywhere.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/736/1*mCuLvuplo2xdmtdU-5MIxA.jpeg)

pin

When I posted that 2024 essay, it was four pages long and handwritten, belonging to my old journal, which I am taking with me. Documenting it made it almost a thousand word essay. I posted it while daydreaming about a day when I will exclaim about my past self being too honest or ridicule myself for being an anonymous person taking pride in sharing something which was part of something personal.

Maybe someday I will finally feel something close to this feeling, or someday later I will feel completely opposite. I am the one who likes the future much more than the present. This future does not involve five years of paying taxes, seven years of having a dog to care for, or ten years of trying to open a publishing house.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/710/1*fP3sGcG6KaHnkTM4qWYAvA.jpeg)

pin

This future is just ten to fifteen days away, I tell you. It is also a future where I know, unlike the rest of the futures I often daydream about, what I will be wearing; where I will be staying, which metro I will be taking, how my glasses will fog up coming out of the air conditioner chamber, and how I will sit and listen and talk to myself about accepting it all, accepting everything I will take myself up to, and accepting that this is what I am becoming, just another being.

text:
JULY 2026

**I don’t know who I am without them.**  
 The clock clicks a moment.  
 **It’s one a.m.,**  
 and I imagine myself calling them back.  
 I see the smile, the tired eyes, the swollen heart.  
 My barren land, my cloudless, clear sky.  
 Rain in my sky, rain I collect in empty bottles.  
 The weaver of gold, the preacher of my life —   
 you are old, and I am not young.

title: Book reviews, because nothing is happening in my life except the fiction I read.
author: samayra
text:
In last week’s article, I said I really didn’t have anything to write. In the piece I wrote months ago, I said when I don’t write, I read, and here I am after reading four books in six days. And… I am also going to stop justifying the actions I take from now on because it’s my article you have decided to read, my account you have stumbled upon, and my words you are reading with your own voice in your head, with or without Spotify. If not, I recommend playing “Blowing Smoke” by Gracie Abrams, which is on repeat in my ears (in both earbuds) while writing this.

First and foremost, with some context, after reading Heaven by Mieko Kawakami… I took a break. I published a piece about it on [Medium](https://medium.com/@se_emdtobego_od/every-book-has-a-time-in-your-life-22182fcc3d4d?sharedUserId=se_emdtobego_od), then my life went on a breakdance. I, well, was lagging in one way or glitching in another. Life had no structure. I was filling things out, including my name and choices like backpacks, clothes, utilities, and colleges, so I wouldn’t end up in a ditch somewhere after four years. I was on Google Maps the most, then mostly in my emails for any updates. Sometimes the dates got extended, and I, well, was living in this hamster wheel for a long while, I believe. But at last, I secured my backup option, and what I want is still in progress, so I am quite stable now. I don’t believe it when I say this.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/1024/0*X4-ZueoV7zr-kuMR.png)

So, yes, we are talking about book reviews. The four books I read included The Vegetarian, Deep Cuts, Lie with Me, and Yesteryear.

When you see the chronological order of reading, you could perfectly assume that I was on a surfboard, balancing with my hands open to the world, dependent on the wind, on tides of emotions that were trying to delve me deeper into a realm I could no longer break through. Did I come out? I don’t know yet, but I feel like I am suspended there, like Billie Eilish on the cover of Hit Me Hard and Soft.

#### **The Vegetarian**

The Vegetarian was recommended by the algorithm itself after I added my review of Heaven.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/1024/0*cq7ypFBEA2aUinSF.png)

It was, like, everywhere. I have known of this book for quite some time before, the red-covered book which I always excused my reading self from because it would take too much time. Additionally, I believed I could finish it in a day. Then you spend the rest of the day convincing yourself you were productive, only to realise what a scaredy-cat you are.

The ultimate truth is, I am scared of books. Of those books, people say, changed the views they had before. That transformed their ideals, their characters in the theatre of life. Big words. I am gatekeeping Sylvia Plath for the same reason. Haven’t read The Bell Jar because my indecisive brain cells, or neurons, believe that they would be unemployed after reading it.

Like how I don’t want to get unemployed in the near future. I hate when I relate everything to myself.

The book starts with the character’s husband, then her brother-in-law (I wished he had just fallen off the balcony), and then her sister. Did I already have a soft spot for her? Why did I, at times, want her to do as they said? Why did I throw the book across the room three times? Why did I want to literally strangle the sister? Why did I relate when I read the same hatred for hospitals or food? Sometimes, I think I should have just said no. Why did I see my reflection so intensely after completing the book in the bathroom? Why didn’t I know about Mongolian birthmarks? I hate the book. Why did I read it now? Well, I just turned eighteen some time before.

I want to answer all these questions. I want to experience everything again. These are my wants, though. What I only need is just another book so that I will be out of this limbo because this book didn’t lead me to write anything but to appreciate everything a little more, sometimes a little less, and realise that I define my own standard of what ‘normal’ means.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/878/0*UslTwxDD6qzQ33GE.png)

#### Deep Cuts

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/735/0*Vvt2t8ZNOMZMgyDL.jpeg)

The next book was Deep Cuts. Thought it was fluff. It turned me into fluff.

Had some other engagements involved in my life, so it took me two and a half days to complete. I don’t like it and don’t hate it; I will probably reread it. It was not the time for this book.

#### Lie with Me

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/252/0*2dcCSsgpWk1aA1k9.jpeg)

Lie with Me… man. I don’t think I have a first love yet. Too young, some say. Too old, some will say.

> *I discovered the pain of waiting because there is this refusal to admit defeat, to believe that a future where it happens again is possible.*

Though my longing was not for a lover, but for a destination.

> *“I’ve probably embellished the scene in retrospect, though I do believe that there are certain men who eclipse everyone else in the room and leave you breathless.*

What heartbreak truly is. Is it a smile on a boy’s face sitting on a grass field? Maybe it is. Maybe I want to believe that it is.

I love the book. I hate monologues. Death is too certain to ever become a choice. I don’t want to be a coward in love. I don’t ever want to be a fool in love.

#### Yesteryear

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/1024/0*AeLQgCE3wvhdAe0g.png)

The last book, this one, was not on my reading list for this month or even this year. Whenever I added a new book to my Goodreads list, this one was always in my recommendations, though I never added it. I already had twenty-one books waiting.

I was already thinking of rereading one of the Harry Potter books (Half-Blood Prince) to cleanse my palate as I was planning to dive into the classic, The Idiot, rather than Crime and Punishment.

But I failed to find my Half-Blood Prince copy. I found it later in the cardboard box where the rest of my school textbooks were. In there, I also found some notebooks. Notebooks with notes, scribbles, rough sheets, and some with a lot of pages left. When I opened one of them, the pristine blankness asked me a question I am afraid of putting into words here.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/1024/0*VtkkwPd6T7UZ8tYN.png)

Yesteryear is among the few books in my life like what Normal People is. And that statement only makes sense to me.

Yesteryear builds different narratives not through people but through the points in time from which they are narrated. When I was trying to write fiction, I used a parallel structure in my storyline.

The main challenge was that I wasn’t fully able to comprehend the ending, even though I was the author of it. I couldn’t arrange the overlapping timelines in a way that made perfect sense to the reader. But Yesteryear did that incredibly well, and it made me envious of the author while reading it.

The story itself was like throwing a stone into a river and watching it skip across the surface. Knowing perfectly well that the next time you won’t be able to do it again, and even if you do, you’ll probably call it luck.

Am I quoting my life right now?

Maybe.

I am.

title: i don’t have anything to write
author: samayra
text:
I really don’t have anything to write. There are no stories left in my world. Even my imagination feels emptier than I ever thought it could. So I am writing here. Maybe if I keep going, I will stumble into something worth writing about.

I don’t know when I started writing with the motive of sharing it on my blogs. When I first began writing, the whole point of it was to remain anonymous. I wanted to write stories, opinions, and articles that were born from my own understanding of a world that never seemed to understand me.

I was probably the worst version of myself then, and writing everything down on my Mac was how I decluttered the mess in my head. Like how you select every file in a folder, right-click, and press **Clean Up By**. Nothing disappeared, but everything found its place.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/1024/0*TC9g5rzE__pslwBD.jpeg)

yekaterina on pinterest commented: Hong Kong always looks so dreamy!!

My life has started to have some structure. Not perfection, just enough order that I am afraid of putting it into words. I am scared of jinxing it, of writing it down and accidentally making it my truth.

I don’t know where or when I realised that words have power. Maybe it was my history teacher in sixth standard, who also taught us geography. Maybe it was my father speaking to one of his acquaintances. Maybe it was a line I borrowed from a book and never returned. I only know that somewhere along the way, I started believing it.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/736/0*zbLwvJO0sqRxOECv.jpeg)

vei on pinterest commented: Как вам «рыбки в пятнах света»? Стоит читать?

Words have power. And maybe in my world, they carry more than that. They are unknown entities, living, breathing, and growing. Because once a word leaves you, you can never really take it back. Even if you refuse to listen to it again, it leaves behind an echo. You can choose not to hold it close to your ear, but you can never become unaware that it exists, that it will always exist between the two of you. Even if one forgets or pretends to. Maybe there is a way to unhear words while keeping your ears open. I haven’t found it yet. The memory always lingers, even when the sound itself is gone.

I know it is selfish to think this way. It almost seems to ridicule the one who got hurt, the one who chose to listen. But isn’t that what all of us do? We forget. So quickly that the hurt no longer feels as sharp when we recount it. The picture remains, but the ache slowly gives up its place.

Perhaps that is why words survive longer than the pain they cause. They keep echoing long after we have convinced ourselves that we have moved on.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/1024/0*7MKDTh3R8SJbfpGC.jpeg)

kate\_ku shared this on pinterest

Maybe I don’t have anything to write because, for the first time, I don’t need writing to survive. Or maybe I no longer need it to make up for the things I didn’t like doing before. I don’t know if I hated those things. It almost feels as though I simply gave up without giving them another try.

I am afraid that writing doesn’t hold that much power over me anymore. Or maybe I am the one refusing to let it. I am afraid that if it stops carrying that weight, I will give this up too. Maybe I am just afraid of trying and finding out the truth. The possibility of that truth has been enough to keep me writing until now.

I mentioned my sixth-grade history teacher earlier. There wasn’t much of a story there. He also taught us geography, which meant that every few pages of my notebook would ask me to draw the map of India again. I never thought much of it then. Recently, though, I found a blog about cartography, and somehow that memory returned.

I never thought much about those maps then. They were exercises, something to fill a page before returning to history. Looking back, I don’t remember whether I drew them well. I only remember drawing the same country over and over again, as though repetition itself could make a place familiar.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/736/0*fbdkhVmaO_5Rmuxe.jpeg)

sen on pinterest commented: where is this plss ? (if this real)

Lately, I have been also thinking about continuity. I write in more than one place now, and because I don’t like publishing the same essay twice, every platform has started keeping a different version of me. One remembers books. Another remembers family. A draft on my Mac remembers something neither of them does. There is also this thing. I have to keep up with both my accounts. It feels like I have no continuation in the story of my life. Maybe I should add an “Already Published” section.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/500/0*r8Ot3hgodQQ65lec.jpeg)

explosion in winter

Then the river might flow more smoothly, rather than in waves or tides of feelings.

Because if someone were to read them all years from now, they would probably think they belonged to different people.

Maybe I don’t need to think about continuity so much. Water doesn’t worry about which river it is in.

Then again, I have spent this entire essay believing that words have power. It would be strange to pretend they are just water now.

used so many maybes!!
